The Erasmus Mundus master in Journalism, Media and Globalisation, run from Aarhus University with partners including Amsterdam, Hamburg, Charles University and City St George's London, has opened applications for the 2027-2029 programme. The deadline is 10 January 2027 at 13:00 CET, and the consortium expects to award 10-15 Erasmus Mundus scholarships.

Programme Highlights

  • One of the longest-running Erasmus Mundus journalism programmes with a global alumni network
  • Specialisation tracks including war and conflict reporting and media and politics
  • Two-year mobility across two European universities with a joint or double degree
  • Scholarships cover both tuition and living costs, open to all nationalities

Who Should Apply

Journalism graduates and working journalists with a bachelor's degree in a relevant subject can apply; strong English documentation and a compelling motivation file matter given the competition for roughly a dozen funded places.

Funding and Costs

Erasmus Mundus scholarships (10-15 expected for the 2027-2029 programme) cover tuition and living costs for the full two years.

Deadline and How to Apply

Applications open from 1 November 2026 on the Mundus Journalism site and close exactly at 13:00 CET on 10 January 2027 — late submissions are not accepted. Key deadline information: 10 January 2027 (13:00 CET); applications opened 1 November 2026.
